back.meaning: Conversational past tense formed with auxiliary (haben/sein) + past participle (Partizip II).

back.meaning: Auxiliary verb used with transitive verbs (taking an accusative object) and static verbs.
back.example_sentence: „Ich habe das Formular gestern unterschrieben.“
back.exam_memory_trick: MEHRHEITS-REGEL: Rund 80% aller deutschen Verben bilden das Perfekt mit 'haben' (alle mit Akkusativ-Objekt!).

back.meaning: Auxiliary verb used with verbs of movement (A -> B), state change, and 3 special kings.

back.exam_memory_trick: SEIN-FORMEL: 1. Ortswechsel (A->B), 2. Zustandswechsel (Schlaf->Wach), 3. Drei Könige (sein, werden, bleiben).

back.meaning: Non-finite verbal form ending the sentence bracket (e.g. gelernt, gefahren).

back.meaning: Structural frame: Auxiliary opens bracket at Position 2, Partizip II closes bracket at sentence end.

back.exam_memory_trick: KLAMMER-MERKVERS: Pos 2 macht die Türe auf, das Partizip ganz hinten schließt den Satz wieder ab!

back.meaning: Prefix + ge- + stem + suffix (-t / -en).

back.meaning: Prefixes be-, ent-, er-, ge-, ver-, zer- form Partizip II WITHOUT 'ge-'.

back.meaning: Verbs of foreign origin ending in -ieren form participle with stem + -t (NO ge-).
